correctness.rationale: Neutrality and discrete cut expansion give A=sum_k(sum_{n_i<=k}w_i)^2>0. The finite-rank free resolvent has G_kappa(i,j)=exp(-kappa|i-j|)/(2J sinh kappa); split rank-one singular part and analytic bounded remainder R0=-D/(2J). The determinant lemma yields scalar F(kappa,eps)=2J sinh kappa -eps w^T(I-eps R_kappa W)^(-1)1=0. Cancellation of w^T1 and Taylor expansion give kappa=A eps^2/(2J^2)+B eps^3/(8J^3)+O(eps^4); J kappa^2 yields the quartic and quintic coefficients. Uniform invertibility for all kappa≥0 and implicit monotonicity near zero excludes other weak-coupling edge states. Unitary alternating-site parity shows H_eps is unitarily equivalent to -H_-eps, yielding the lower-edge expansion and odd-power gap difference. Sup spectrum is convex in eps and at least 2J, so strict weak-coupling binding on each sign persists for all nonzero coupling. Independent high-precision secular-root calculations on the neutral defect (0,1),(1,-2),(5,1) reproduced A=5 B=-32 and approached predicted fifth-order coefficient -20; numerical approximation is corroboration, not universal proof.
